front: Why is the solution set of $Ax=b$ ($b\ne0$) not a subspace?
back: It does not contain $\mathbf 0$ (and is not closed under addition); it is a shifted copy of the null space.

front: Column space of $A$ and its link to $Ax=b$
back: $\operatorname{col}(A)=\{Ax\}$, the span of the columns. $Ax=b$ is exactly solvable iff $b\in\operatorname{col}(A)$.

front: Define a basis and the dimension
back: A basis is an independent list that spans the space (minimal spanning set = maximal independent set). The dimension is the number of vectors in any basis.

Matrix of a map in a new basis; what is preserved?
back: $\tilde M=S^{-1}MS$ (similar matrices). Eigenvalues, trace, determinant and rank are unchanged.

front: What does $Q^\top Q=I$ say, and what follows?
back: Columns are orthonormal. If $Q$ is square, $Q^{-1}=Q^\top$, and $\|Qx\|=\|x\|$, angles are preserved.
$c_i=q_i^\top x$, just dot products, no linear system to solve.

Why must the error $x-Px$ be orthogonal to the subspace?
back: Otherwise a small move inside the subspace would reduce the distance. The condition $A^\top(x-A\lambda)=0$ gives the normal equations.
